newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market thin at $65 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market thin at $65 - feedlots.

text.p: Trading was light at prices steady with last week's top prices on Monday at U.S. Plains cattle feedlots, with most in the industry gearing down for the Christmas holiday on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
Packers reportedly had sufficient inventory for this week's operations, but need to start buying Thursday for the upcoming New Year's holiday week, they said.

About 3,000 head sold in Kansas at $65.00 per cwt, according to USDA and private sources. The sales were steady with the bulk of last week's sales. No sales were reported in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area.

The Panhandle area showlist was estimated near 61,000 head, down 4,500 from last week, sources there said. Kansas' showlist was pegged near 73,400 head, down 1,500 from last week, sources in that area said.

Fed cattle prices were expected to be supported in the near term by an outlook for firm beef prices through the holidays as retailers book shipments for planned promotions during the first half of January, some sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.34 to $0.67 per cwt on 45 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
